newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RAVANELLI INJURY NOT AS BAD AS FEARED SAYS ROBSON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAVANELLI INJURY NOT AS BAD AS FEARED SAYS ROBSON.

text.p: Middlesbrough's Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli may be fit for the F.A. Cup final against Chelsea on May 17, coach Bryan Robson said on Tuesday.
Robson, interviewed at a race meeting in Chester, said Ravanelli's injury was "not as bad as first thought".

The striker, who cost 7.0 million pounds ($11.3 million) from Juventus last year, limped off after 34 minutes of Middlesbrough's 3-3 draw at Manchester United on Sunday, clutching the back of his left leg.
He underwent a scan on what proved to be a hamstring injury on Tuesday and Robson said the injury was not as serious as first feared.
"It's not snapped," said Robson. "...hopefully, we can get him fit for Wembley."
However, the 31-goal striker will miss Middlesbrough's last two league matches of the season at Blackburn on Thursday and at Leeds on Sunday.
